insights.concise_text: The comparative analysis of BERT, XLNet and RoBERTa on speculation detection and scope resolution uses the Khandelwal and Sawant (BIBREF12) methodology modified to support experimentation with multiple models.

triple.subject: comparative analysis of BERT, XLNet and RoBERTa
triple.object: the methodology by Khandelwal and Sawant (BIBREF12) modified to support experimentation with multiple models

insights.concise_text: The single dataset training approach that outperforms all existing systems on speculation detection and scope resolution reports results as an average of 5 runs of the model.

triple.subject: single dataset training approach
triple.object: an average of 5 runs of the model

insights.concise_text: The inter-dataset scores used to test generalizability show BF gets the best results when trained on BA, while BF has 2670 sentences and BA has 11871 sentences.

triple.subject: inter-dataset scores
triple.object: BF gets the best results when trained on BA

insights.concise_text: Jointly training on multiple datasets, which improves performance over single dataset training on most datasets, reports results as an average of 3 runs of the model.

triple.subject: training on multiple datasets
triple.object: an average of 3 runs of the model

insights.concise_text: The observation that XLNet consistently outperforms RoBERTa on speculation detection and scope resolution is confirmed by applying the 2 models to negation detection and scope resolution.

triple.subject: XLNet consistently outperforming RoBERTa
triple.object: negation detection and scope resolution

insights.concise_text: State-of-the-art results on three of four datasets on the negation scope resolution task correspond to BF, BA and SFU datasets.

triple.subject: three of four datasets on the negation scope resolution task
triple.object: BF, BA and SFU datasets

insights.concise_text: Because tokens could be different for different models, the Average method averages output vectors for each token that the word was split into by the model's tokenizer.

triple.subject: tokens could be different for different models
triple.object: the Average method to average output vectors for each token that the word was split into by the model's tokenizer

insights.concise_text: The word ‘tomorrow' split into 3 tokens, ‘tom', ‘##or' and ‘##row', is handled by First Token using the output vector corresponding to ‘tom'.

triple.subject: First Token
triple.object: the output vector corresponding to ‘tom' for ‘tomorrow'

insights.concise_text: For fair comparison across BERT, XLNet and RoBERTa, only the tokenizer and the model are changed while the same hyperparameters are used for the entire architecture for all 3 models.

triple.subject: fair comparison across BERT, XLNet and RoBERTa
triple.object: only the tokenizer and the model to be changed

insights.concise_text: The subtasks we experiment on are sequence labelling tasks, and the pre-training objective of XLNet may capture long-term dependencies better, essential for sequence labelling tasks.

triple.object: sequence labelling tasks
